subject: Token accounting windows and commit structure for Hosted API
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme.ai>, Acme Robotics Procurement <procure@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-06-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify: how do you count streaming and rounding?

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo — team liked the throughput numbers. Before we move to procurement, Procurement and Eng have a couple of specific questions about how usage is measured for billing:

- For streaming responses (server->client partial tokens): do you bill tokens as they are generated, or at the end of a response?
- If a single request streams 1.2 tokens on average (short bursts), how is rounding handled? Per-request or per-minute window?
- For our committed tier discussion, we also need the definition of "billable tokens" in contract language so we can map it to our internal forecasting.

Can you send suggested contract wording and the practical examples that procurement will accept? Alicia will be coordinating legal.

Appreciate it — Jordan
Jordan Lee
Head of Platform & AI
Acme Robotics

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-06-10T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: how do you count streaming and rounding?

Jordan — great to reconnect. Short answers up front: we bill on generated tokens (not bytes), streaming tokens are counted as they are generated by the model, and rounding is performed per-second aggregation with a 0.5-token round-up rule for billing purposes in our Hosted plans. Below I put suggested contract wording and two worked examples so procurement/legal have something concrete. Looping Ben & Rishi for discount/commit commentary.

Suggested contract wording (draft):
"Billable Tokens" means the aggregate number of model-generated tokens produced in response to Customer requests to the Redwood Hosted API during the applicable billing period. For streamed responses, tokens are counted at the time they are produced by the model and recorded against the Customer's usage ledger. For purposes of invoicing, Redwood aggregates generated tokens in one-second billing windows; partial-token sums within any single window are rounded up to the next 0.5 token.

Practical examples:
- Example A (short streaming burst): a single response emits 3 partial chunks across 0.4s that accumulate to 1.2 generated tokens. Since the total occurs within a single one-second window, we round 1.2 -> 1.5 billable tokens.
- Example B (longer dialogue): a long streaming response spans 2.3s and emits 4.7 tokens in the first second and 2.1 in the next. We bill 4.7 -> 5.0 (first sec) and 2.1 -> 2.5 (second sec) for a total 7.5 billable tokens.

Notes and negotiable items:
- We can change the rounding granularity for committed enterprise customers (e.g., per-request rounding or per-minute windows) as part of a tiered commit.
- For reserved commit tiers, we define "Net Billable Tokens" as Billable Tokens less any cache-hit reductions and system-initiated retries; we can provide monthly CSV usage ledgers that map raw generated tokens to billed quantities.

I'm attaching a redline-capable term sheet and a sample usage ledger export. Ben, Rishi — do we want to propose any special rounding or aggregation setting in the committed pricing proposal for Acme?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-term-sheet-acme-v2.pdf (term sheet, editable)
Attachment: sample-usage-ledgers-q1.csv (sample CSV)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-06-10T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: how do you count streaming and rounding?

Thanks Laura — nice tidy examples. Jordan, from a pricing perspective we typically offer two paths for customers with predictable throughput:

1) Volume discount (no commit): standard per-token price with stepped discounts at 10M / 50M / 200M billable-token thresholds, rounding stays at our Hosted default (1s window, 0.5 token).
2) Commit tier (monthly commit): committed tokens purchased at a deeper discounted rate; we can make rounding and aggregation contractually per-request (which typically benefits high-burst streaming use cases) or keep per-second aggregation if you prefer more conservative accounting. Any unused committed tokens can be rolled into a 3-month carry-forward at a reduced carryover rate.

If Acme wants per-request rounding, we would set a commit floor at the 50M level for contract economics and offer a 12% additional discount on top of the commit price. For smaller commits (10M), we can offer a 6% extra discount but keep the 1s rounding.

Happy to run a modeled invoice if you share a month of sample generated-token exports (we've attached a sample ledger).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme.ai>, Acme Robotics Procurement <procure@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-06-10T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: how do you count streaming and rounding?

Thanks Laura and Ben — that helps. A couple follow-ups from procurement: 

- Procurement wants definitive contract text for "Net Billable Tokens", including how caching and retries are handled and an explicit CSV format example.
- Legal would like the rounding logic to be expressed as a deterministic algorithm (not prose). Example: "Let G_t be generated tokens in second t; billable tokens = sum_t ceil(2 * G_t)/2".

Also, our engineering team prefers per-request rounding for streaming because it maps to our client instrumentation. If we accept a 12% add-on discount at 50M commit as you suggested, we'd like that per-request rounding language in the SOW.

Can you draft the exact contract snippets (legal-ready) and confirm whether the monthly usage ledger we receive will include raw generated tokens, per-second aggregated counts, and final billed tokens?

Jordan
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-10T15:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: how do you count streaming and rounding?

Jordan — happy to do the legal-ready snippets. Laura / Ben — proposed compromise: offer Acme per-request rounding for the 50M commit with the 12% incremental discount. Add explicit CSV columns in the SOW: timestamp, request_id, raw_generated_tokens, per_second_aggregate, billed_tokens. We will also include a short appendix that defines the rounding function as Ben suggested: billed_tokens_per_second = ceil(2 * G_t)/2, and billed_tokens_request = sum over seconds within request window of that per-second billed amount (if per-request rounding is chosen).

We should confirm whether Acme needs on-demand proofs (e.g., monthly audit export + SHA256 hash of ledger) — that sometimes comes up in procurement for regulated partners.

If that sounds good, I'll draft a contract exhibit and send to your procurement legal alias.

—Rishi

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme.ai>, Acme Robotics Procurement <procure@acme.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-11T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: how do you count streaming and rounding?

Jordan / Alicia — attaching the contract exhibit and sample CSV with the columns Rishi proposed. Key points in the exhibit:

- Definition: Billable Tokens counted as model-generated tokens.
- Rounding: default per-second window with 0.5-token granularity unless Customer elects per-request rounding as part of a commit.
- Commit offer: 50M/month commit -> additional 12% off commit rate, per-request rounding enabled, 3-month 50% carryforward (unused tokens discounted).
- Audit: monthly ledger export in CSV + SHA256 hash; we can support a one-time audit at Customer expense.

Next steps: Alicia, if procurement/legal are OK with the exhibit I'll issue a DocuSign term sheet with the pricing lines and SOW addendum. Link to draft DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/transaction/abc123-ds

Thanks — Laura
